title: The morning after the midterms: Iran reads the vote, and talks stall in Doha
summary: Iran says US voters rejected the war as Democrats take Congress and Trump pushes back, Doha talks end without a breakthrough while more tankers are hit around Hormuz, another 310-drone night over Ukraine, a White House meeting on the Oleshky truce, and the Theodore Roosevelt still in the South China Sea.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Wednesday, November fourth. The morning after the US midterm elections. And the results are already being read as a statement about the Iran war.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. Projections show Democrats taking both houses of Congress. And Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who is also Tehran's chief negotiator, posted that Americans had said, in capital letters, no to war.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: He also warned Washington it would face what he called a nightmare if it ignored its voters.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And President Trump disagreed with that reading. He told Fox News he didn't think the result was about the war. He said it was gasoline prices. And asked by CBS whether the war would now end, he said, quote, it'll end when I say it ends.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So both sides are claiming the vote supports their position.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And meanwhile the negotiations themselves have hit a wall, at least for now. Iran says the US reply to its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz was, quote, unconvincing.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Those indirect talks in Doha ended without a breakthrough. Qatar says both sides remain committed to the process, though. And Trump confirmed the strikes on Qeshm Island that we talked about yesterday.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The ones US officials called limited and defensive, after Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired at an American aircraft.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And at sea, the pattern continues. On Tuesday, the British maritime agency UKMTO reported two attacks on ships in the strait. In one, a tanker's engine room was hit by two unknown projectiles, about fourteen nautical miles northeast of Limah, on Oman's coast. No casualties reported.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Then today the Revolutionary Guard claimed four tankers were destroyed by mines in what it calls a prohibited lane south of the strait, and that two more ships were detained.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Same caveat as every day this week. Nobody has been able to verify whether Iran's claims match the incidents UKMTO actually reported. Central Command has said the main lanes are cleared of mines.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's head to Ukraine, where the strikes on the power grid haven't let up.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Overnight, Ukraine's air force says Russia launched three hundred and ten drones, and eighty-one of them were jet-powered. Two hundred and seventy-two were brought down. But strikes still hit nineteen locations.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Odesa, a shopping centre caught fire. Two people were injured in Dnipro. And energy sites in western Ukraine were hit, including in Ternopil.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's on top of Monday night's barrage, which Ukraine's energy officials called the biggest attack on the grid this year. And the guided bomb strike on the aid centre in Komyshuvakha, where the death toll stood at thirty-three.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line, the General Staff reported two hundred and eight clashes on Tuesday. Kostiantynivka was again the busiest sector, with twenty-four Russian attacks. And Russia dropped about a hundred and sixty guided bombs in fifty airstrikes.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And Ukraine's strikes inside Russia are still burning, literally. Kyiv Post reports the fire at the big Samara oil hub, the one hit on Monday, was still going a day later. That's on top of the Yaroslavl refinery strike.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now, there's an unusual diplomatic thread here. The First Lady's office says Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House tomorrow, Thursday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The topic is that local ceasefire around Oleshky, in Kherson region. The six-day truce that let aid in and residents out, which she's credited with brokering.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Reports differ on exactly who's attending. And when asked, the Kremlin's spokesman said he knew nothing about it. Separately, working-level Russia and Ukraine talks are planned in Abu Dhabi on November tenth and eleventh.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So two tracks. A narrow humanitarian one at the White House, and the bigger negotiation in Abu Dhabi.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Quick lap of the other fronts. Yemen. On Tuesday the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three drones, one of them over the Mecca region. A Houthi spokesman claimed strikes on Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base, in Khamis Mushait. And then, confusingly, the same spokesman said the group hadn't attacked Saudi territory that day.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So that one's still unresolved.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Gaza, AFP reports Israeli strikes near Khan Younis and Gaza City on Tuesday killed at least four people, including a seventeen-year-old girl. Israel's military says it struck militants in al-Mawasi.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And then the ships. The Theodore Roosevelt is still in the South China Sea. Chinese commercial satellite imagery published today appears to show the carrier group there, consistent with this week's USNI fleet tracker.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Navy hasn't said when it will enter the Indian Ocean. It's reportedly heading for the Middle East to relieve another carrier. The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush remain in the Arabian Sea.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, what to watch. How the White House responds to Iran calling its reply unconvincing, and whether there's another round in Doha. Tomorrow's meeting on Oleshky, and the Abu Dhabi talks next week. And whether the Roosevelt shows up west of the Strait of Malacca.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
